name: Building licensing, approvals and the building code
what: Hold a builder's or building practitioner's licence or registration, get building approval and inspections from a council or private certifier, and build to the National Construction Code and each state's variations.

layers.who: Australian Building Codes Board (National Construction Code)
State building law and variations to the code
Local council or private building certifier

consistency_note: One national code adopted by each state with its own variations; licensing and approvals differ by state.

basis.quote: State, territory and local governments set the rules for construction licences and permits.
The design and construction of buildings, structures, plumbing and drainage systems must follow the National Construction Code .

issues.what: States vary the National Construction Code and assess compliance differently, so builders working in several states meet different standards.

evidence.source: Housing construction productivity: Can we fix it?
evidence.quote: The implementation of the NCC varies across states and territories. There are deviations from the agreed NCC ruleset across jurisdictions as well as differences in how compliance is assessed. This has resulted in inconsistency in construction standards.

issues.what: Some councils add their own design and materials rules on top of the building code.

evidence.source: Housing construction productivity: Can we fix it?
evidence.quote: some local governments impose rules that affect how homes are built, including rules around external design and building materials, which overlap with the NCC. This adds complexity for construction firms who want to, or do, operate across multiple jurisdictions

issues.what: The building code runs to more than 2,000 pages and changes every three years, with no single list of what a builder must comply with.

evidence.source: Housing construction productivity: Can we fix it?
evidence.quote: The National Construction Code and related housing provisions are more than 2,000 pages long.

evidence.source: Housing construction productivity: Can we fix it?
evidence.quote: Code updates are currently scheduled every three years.

issues.what: Builders' licences are state-based; automatic mutual recognition helps, but not every state has joined and exemptions remain.

evidence.source: Housing construction productivity: Can we fix it?
evidence.quote: not all jurisdictions have signed up. Many exemptions and conditions still exist.

evidence.locator: Section C (Occupational licensing), key points, p. 89
evidence.quote: Not all states have joined the automatic mutual recognition scheme (Queensland does not participate), and states and territories continue to exclude some professions.

issues.status_note: Automatic mutual recognition of occupational licences now operates in most jurisdictions; Queensland does not take part (PC 2025).
